name: magazine
title: The magazine insert: follower, serpentine spring and a snap-in cap in one piece
orientation: Flat on the bed, the follower at the bottom of the picture, the cap at the top. Drop discs into the column from the top, then press the insert in after them until its hooks click into the walls' notches; a firm pull on the cap lifts it out to reload.

width.rule: The spring's height off the bed: half the body's working width, pressing the follower's middle

across.rule: The follower and top bar across the column

follower_w.rule: The follower along the barrel: wider than the disc, so it rests on the column's ledge when the magazine is empty

ledge.rule: The column's ledge each side of its mouth, which the follower sits on when empty

bar.rule: The cap bar: tall enough to stand above the body's top edge, to be gripped

spring.rule: Each leaf of the serpentine along the barrel: the disc's diameter

turns.rule: Leaves in the serpentine: enough gaps to close by the preload and the stroke

preload.rule: How much the spring is squeezed with the magazine empty: the feed force on the last disc comes from this

stroke.rule: The follower's travel from the ledge (empty) to the top of a full stack resting on the sled: six discs less the slot's half-height, less the ledge's height above the slot's centre

compression.rule: How much the spring is squeezed in the drawing: 0 as printed, preload when empty, preload + stroke when full (the leaves are drawn closer, not bowed)

overlap.rule: How far the plates sink into the end leaves, so they join

hook.rule: Each snap hook's leaf, hanging from the cap's end down the column wall: long enough that the barb's deflection stays under the strain limit

hook_root.rule: The block each hook grows from, sunk into the cap

undercut.rule: How far each barb stands out past the cap's edge: the hooks' root blocks sit inside the edge, so the barb reaches the wall and into its notch

lead.rule: The barbs' lead faces: pressing the cap in deflects them

back.rule: The barbs' backs: as sloped as their leads, so the cap pulls out with about the push that seated it (well over the spring's push); 90 would hold for good
